table.rotateHint: Turn your phone sideways to see the table and your hand at once.

ukeire.desc: The tiles that would improve your hand if drawn next — fewer kinds and copies mean a narrower path to tenpai. The efficiency trainer counts it after every discard.

tedashi.desc: A discard pulled from your hand rather than the tile you just drew. It reveals more about your hand than a tsumogiri does, since it shows you chose to keep the drawn tile instead.

tsumogiri.desc: Discarding the tile you just drew, untouched. It gives away less information than a tedashi, because your hand shape didn't visibly change.

shanten.desc: How many tile exchanges a hand needs to reach tenpai. 0 means already tenpai (waiting to win); -1 means already won.

genbutsu.desc: A tile provably safe against a specific riichi: it's already in that player's own discards, or someone discarded it after their riichi without being ronned. The only tier that's actually 100% safe.

suji.desc: A tile whose matching ryanmen (two-sided wait) is ruled out because its genbutsu counterpart three away is already safe (e.g. 4 is suji if 1 is genbutsu). It only rules out that one wait shape — tanki, shanpon and kanchan waits on the same tile are untouched.

dora.desc: A bonus-value tile indicated by the dora indicator (the next tile after it in sequence). It adds to a hand's han but is not itself a yaku — a hand needs a real yaku to win even with dora.

uraDora.desc: A second, hidden dora indicator revealed only for hands that win by riichi. It rewards riichi specifically, on top of whatever yaku and dora the hand already has.

efficiency.title: Efficiency trainer
efficiency.desc: Pick the best discard; see the tiles that improve your hand.
efficiency.intro: Each round deals you a real hand mid-match. Discard the tile that keeps your hand closest to tenpai and keeps the most ways to improve it (its ukeire). After you discard, the trainer shows whether it was the best choice and how many tiles you left on the table.

shanten.title: Shanten trainer
shanten.desc: Guess how far a hand is from tenpai, against the clock.
shanten.intro: You're shown a hand and asked to guess its shanten: how many tile exchanges it needs to reach tenpai (0 = already waiting to win). Hands stream continuously, so answer quickly and move on to the next.

scoring.title: Scoring trainer
scoring.desc: Guess han, fu and points for a winning hand.
scoring.intro: You're shown a completed, winning hand. Work out its yaku, han, fu and the resulting points before checking the answer — the skill scoring trainers are built for.

folding.title: Folding trainer
folding.desc: Someone declared riichi. Pick the safest tile to throw.
folding.intro: An opponent has declared riichi and you're not in a position to push. Pick the discard least likely to deal into their hand, using only public information (their discards and everyone else's) — never what they're actually holding.

reason.genbutsu: they threw it themselves, so they are furiten on it
reason.noChance: every tile a run to it would need is already accounted for
reason.oneChance: only one copy is left of what a run to it would need
reason.doubleSuji: both suji partners are in their discards
reason.suji: its suji partner is in their discards
reason.halfSuji: only one side is suji — the ryanmen on the other side is still live
reason.nonSuji: nothing on the table rules it out

caveat.genbutsu: Genbutsu is the only real safety: they discarded it, so they cannot ron it.
caveat.suji: Suji only rules out a ryanmen. A tanki, shanpon, kanchan or penchan on this tile still wins.
caveat.kabe: A wall only rules out runs. A tanki or shanpon on this tile still wins.
caveat.general: Nothing below genbutsu is safe — it is only less likely.

folding.hindsight: A tile from the safest tier still counts as correct even when it turns out to be in the wait — nothing on the table said otherwise.
